age.evidence: Adult male and female 3-8 month-old WT and global βArr1-KO... WT and global βArr2-KO... WT and VMAT2-HET mice

sex.evidence: Adult male and female 3-8 month-old WT and global βArr1-KO... mice

dosing.evidence: The vehicle for lisuride... consisted of N,N-dimethyllacetamide (final volume 0.5%)... and it was brought to volume with 5% 2-hydroxypropylβ-cyclodextrin in sterile water... All drugs were injected (i.p.) in a 5 ml/kg volume.

LSD-tartrate (NIDA Drug Supply Program)... The vehicle for lisuride, LSD, MDL, reserpine, SCH23390, and GR127935 consisted of N,N-dimethyllacetamide... 5% 2-hydroxypropylβ-cyclodextrin... All drugs were injected (i.p.)

group_housing.evidence: Mice were housed 3-5 per cage according to sex and genotype

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12:12 h light:dark cycle (lights on 0700 h)... Behavioral experiments were conducted between 0900-1700 h

assays.assay_description: 21×21×30 cm clear Plexiglas arena; locomotor distance, vertical rearing counts and stereotypy counts recorded in 5-min bins for 30 min baseline + 90 min post-injection.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were placed into the open field, 30 min later they were injected... and immediately returned to the open field for 90 min (baseline is data collection, not habituation)

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed into the open field... freely moving

food_restriction.evidence: Plexiglas arena; no food in the apparatus during recording

water_restriction.evidence: Plexiglas arena; no water in the apparatus during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: injected... and immediately returned to the open field for 90 min

outcomes.summary: Lisuride dose-dependently reduced cumulative locomotor and rearing activities in both βArr1 and βArr2 mice. Stereotypies showed a U-shaped dose-response. Locomotion was lower overall in KO than WT animals.
outcomes.statistics: Locomotion: two-way ANOVA genotype [F(1,161)=4.050, p=0.046], treatment [F(7,161)=33.270, p<0.001]; βArr2 genotype [F(1,157)=11.710, p<0.001]. Rearing ANCOVA treatment [F(7,160)=27.412, p<0.001]. Stereotypy ANCOVA [F(7,160)=14.609, p<0.001].
outcomes.evidence: With lisuride, locomotion in both genotypes decreased in a dose-dependent fashion from 0.01 to 0.5 mg/kg lisuride relative to vehicle (p-values ≤ 0.005)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Fusion Integra software recorded locomotor activity (distance traveled), rearing (vertical beam-breaks), and stereotypical activities

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Fusion Integra software recorded... in 5-min blocks

B4_ethological.evidence: rearing (vertical counts) is a natural ethological behaviour

D2_session_duration.evidence: 30 min baseline + 90 min post-injection = continuous recording in apparatus

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline activities were monitored from 0 to 30 min

assays.assay_description: Head twitches scored manually (Observer XT 16) during the first 30 min post-injection of vehicle, LSD (0.3 mg/kg), or lisuride (0.01-4 mg/kg), filmed during open field test.

setup_habituation.evidence: filmed during the motor activity test; no separate apparatus habituation

time_to_assay.evidence: scored over the initial 30-min post-injection period

outcomes.summary: Lisuride produced very few HTRs (<7/30 min even at 4 mg/kg) in both βArr1 and βArr2 mice. By contrast, LSD (0.3 mg/kg) robustly induced HTRs in WT and βArr1-KOs but the effect was lost in βArr2-KOs.
outcomes.evidence: Even with this high 4 mg/kg dose less than 7 HTRs were identified over the 30-min post-injection period

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours in rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: scored by observers using Observer XT 16 (manual scoring)

assays.assay_description: Hunched posture, paw kneading, rigid posture, flat posture, Staub tail, and tremor/body shaking scored manually (Observer XT 16) during first 30 min post-injection in open field.

setup_habituation.evidence: filmed during open field motor test

time_to_assay.evidence: scored over the initial 30-min post-injection period

outcomes.summary: Lisuride dose-dependently increased 5-HT syndrome-associated behaviors, particularly in WT mice. βArr2-KOs showed markedly reduced responses across 0.05-4 mg/kg, while βArr1-KOs only showed reduction at 4 mg/kg.
outcomes.evidence: Within WT mice 5-HT syndrome-associated responses were expressed at higher levels with 0.05, 0.1, 1, 2 and 4 mg/kg lisuride than vehicle

B1_num_measures.evidence: hunched posture, repetitive paw kneading, rigid posture, flat posture, Staub tail, and tremor or body shaking

B4_ethological.evidence: natural ethological postures/responses (paw kneading, Staub tail, tremor)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: scored by observers blinded using Observer XT 16 (manual)

assays.assay_description: Time spent grooming scored (TopScan) over the first 30 min post-injection in the open field.

time_to_assay.evidence: scored over the initial 30-min post-injection period

outcomes.summary: Lisuride decreased grooming in βArr1 mice (0.05-1, 4 mg/kg) but produced an inverted U-shaped response in βArr2 mice (increase at 0.05-0.5 mg/kg, decrease at 4 mg/kg).
outcomes.statistics: p ≤ 0.030 for βArr1 doses; p = 0.021 for βArr2 0.05 mg/kg increase; p = 0.006 for βArr2 4 mg/kg decrease
outcomes.evidence: time spent grooming in βArr1 mice decreased with 0.05-1 and 4 mg/kg lisuride... In βArr2 animals lisuride produced an inverted U-shaped function

B4_ethological.evidence: grooming is a natural ethological behaviour

assays.assay_description: Number of retrograde walking events scored (TopScan) over the first 30 min post-injection in the open field.

time_to_assay.evidence: scored over the initial 30-min post-injection period

outcomes.summary: Retrograde walking showed a biphasic U-shaped dose-response in both βArr1 and βArr2 mice — decreased at low/mid doses then increased at 2-4 mg/kg.
outcomes.statistics: p < 0.001 for low-dose decreases; p ≤ 0.021 for high-dose increases
outcomes.evidence: Retrograde walking assumed a biphasic U-shaped curve across doses

B4_ethological.evidence: retrograde walking not a typical natural ethological behaviour

assays.assay_description: Acoustic startle and PPI in SR-LAB chambers; 10 min habituation followed by 42 trials (null, pulse-alone, prepulse-pulse at 4/8/12 dB). %PPI calculated. Tested with lisuride alone and with antagonists (MDL100907, raclopride, clozapine, SCH23390, GR127935).

setup_habituation.evidence: After 10 min of habituation to a white-noise background (64 dB)

setup_restrain.evidence: PPI startle chamber (SR-LAB) — rubric lists PPI startle chambers with body-restraint tubes as restrained

time_to_assay.evidence: Following drug administration, the animals were placed into the PPI apparatus. After 10 min of habituation... a series of 42 trials was given

outcomes.summary: Lisuride (0.5 mg/kg) disrupted PPI in βArr1 mice but not βArr2 mice. MDL100907 failed to rescue PPI; raclopride normalized PPI only in WT, not in βArr1-KOs. Clozapine, SCH23390, and GR127935 normalized PPI in both βArr1 genotypes.
outcomes.evidence: 0.5 mg/kg lisuride reduced PPI overall relative to all treatment groups (p-values ≤ 0.007)

B1_num_measures.evidence: %PPI, null activity, and startle activity examined

B4_ethological.evidence: PPI startle is explicitly not ethological in rubric

D2_session_duration.evidence: 42 trials with 80 ms ISI — short PPI session; duration not explicitly stated

assays.assay_description: Two-bottle choice in home cage. Days 1: water-water baseline; Day 2: vehicle + sucrose-water; Day 3: lisuride (1 mg/kg i.p.) + sucrose-water; Days 4-6: sucrose-water. 2-h sessions after 4 h fluid restriction.

application_type.evidence: administered 1 mg/kg lisuride (i.p.) and 5 min later were given S-W

setup_habituation.evidence: mice housed individually for 7 days prior; metering bottles filled with water repeated until consumption stable with no side-bias

water_restriction.evidence: water bottle was removed 2.5 h from the home-cage before the beginning of the dark cycle... 4 h total fluid deprivation

time_to_assay.evidence: administered 1 mg/kg lisuride (i.p.) and 5 min later were given S-W

outcomes.summary: VMAT2-HET mice showed no sucrose preference on Day 2 (anhedonia). A single lisuride dose on Day 3 robustly increased preference in VMAT2-HETs, persisting on Day 4, then declining to vehicle levels by Days 5-6. WTs maintained preference throughout.
outcomes.evidence: VMAT2-HETs' sucrose preference exceeded WTs (p=0.003) and was significantly higher from their selections on days 1 and 2... by days 5 and 6 sucrose preference in VMAT2-HET mice fell from WT levels

B1_num_measures.evidence: sucrose preference and total fluid intake

B4_ethological.evidence: preference score from volumes; not a scored ethological act

E1_environment_type.evidence: VMAT2 mice were housed individually... pair of bottles was presented to mice

E2_shelter.evidence: standard home cage; no specific shelter mentioned

E8_food_water.evidence: Food was available ad libitum; bottles of sucrose/water during test

D4_baseline.evidence: The final W-W pairing occurred on day 1; vehicle S-W on day 2

D5_followup.evidence: S-W pairings days 4-6, ≥24 h after lisuride dosing on day 3

assays.assay_description: 6-min tail suspension via Med Associates hook + load cell measuring immobility. Tested acutely (30 min post-injection, or 2 h post-LSD) and on days 1, 3, 5 post-injection in VMAT2 mice and reserpinized C57BL/6J mice.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were suspended by the tail for 6 min using medical tape attached to a Med Associates tail suspension hook

time_to_assay.evidence: tested 30 min later... LSD tested 2 h later... tested 30 min and 1, 3, or 5 days later

outcomes.summary: In VMAT2-HETs, acute 0.5 mg/kg lisuride, LSD, and fluoxetine all reduced immobility vs vehicle; lisuride and LSD effects were lost by day 1 while fluoxetine persisted to day 1. 1 mg/kg lisuride was ineffective in HETs and increased immobility in WTs at day 1. In reserpinized C57BL/6J mice, 0.5 mg/kg lisuride reduced immobility at 24 h.
outcomes.evidence: In VMAT2-HETs acute administration of fluoxetine, LSD, or 0.5 mg/kg lisuride reduced immobility times compared to vehicle (p-values ≤ 0.043)

B4_ethological.evidence: immobility in tail suspension is not ethological per rubric

D1_continuity.evidence: tested acutely and on days 1, 3, and 5

D2_session_duration.evidence: suspended by the tail for 6 min

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline tail suspension reported

D5_followup.evidence: responses assessed on days 1, 3, and 5 post-injection

judge_notes: Merged candidates that listed Open Field, HTR, 5-HT syndrome, grooming, and retrograde walking — kept these as 5 separate assays per gptoss/glm because each measures a distinct behavioural domain even though all were filmed during the same recording session.
PPI scored as setup_restrain=yes because rubric explicitly lists 'PPI startle chambers with body-restraint tubes' as restrained.
Open Field setup_habituation = no: the 30-min pre-injection period was a recorded baseline (data collected), not a habituation without data collection.
Sucrose preference: scored as Yes for setup_habituation because mice were habituated to two-bottle drinking until intake was stable and no side-bias detected.

B7 (automated classification) scored 0 for all assays per rubric — Fusion Integra is beam-break and TopScan is centroid-tracking based on the description; neither qualifies as behavioural classification.
Tail Suspension D1 corrected to 1 (Multiple discrete sessions across days 1, 3, 5) — gptoss had inconsistent score=0 with value 'Multiple discrete sessions'.
Dosing for LSD includes both 0.3 mg/kg (HTR comparison) and 0.5 mg/kg (TST comparison) doses as listed in the paper.
